scope: Read-only production code/dependency/database review plus isolated loopback experiments. No real model retry, production/test source edit, environment/system-network change or daily data mutation.
supplier_feedback_boundary: User reports supplier observed requester-side disconnection; this review does not infer upstream model unavailability from a RemoteProtocolError.
confirmed_findings: All four failures followed the last decoded HTTP body chunk by 49.70879–50.01547 seconds. This is body-decoder timing, not packet-level idle proof.
No recorded first-event, 300-second semantic idle, 900-second hard, child or parent deadline was reached. All four lack a terminal event and stay below byte/event limits.
ModelClient explicitly passes HTTPX read=None. Installed httpcore passes this through AnyIO; no 50-second read timer was found in the examined application/HTTPX/httpcore paths.
Application task cancellation and idle timeout were distinguishable in controlled runs and retained cancellation attribution.

Direct client.aclose during a pending HTTP or TLS read yields ReadError without cancelled_by in the current diagnostic schema. The production runtime normally cancels/awaits children before closing their clients.

Explicit local socket receive-shutdown and a local forwarding proxy closing after its idle timer both reproduced RemoteProtocolError with cancelled_by=null. The exception type is not a causal attribution.
HTTP and verified TLS direct loopback requests both survived 55 seconds without bytes and then returned a complete terminal plus HTTP EOF.
httpcore emits receive_response_body.failed before its exception-cleanup response_closed event. The application currently drops response_closed events from its bounded trace list.
Active HTTP/1.1 requests clear keepalive expiry; a fresh CONNECT occurred in one actual failure while the others reused connections, so a reuse-only explanation is insufficient.
hypotheses_not_proven: A roughly 50-second body-idle policy in the local proxy or its selected transport path can explain both the supplier-side requester-disconnect observation and the application exception. Its exact enforcing component remains unproven by these records.
Uninstrumented socket/transport shutdown can leave cancelled_by null; no application raw-socket shutdown call was found and normal Runtime.close ordering does not currently supply a matching trigger.
A cleanup exception could theoretically replace the primary failure. The performed controls did not reproduce that, so it is not a demonstrated explanation.

repair_points_after_causal_confirmation.change: Add bounded type-only receive_response_body.failed, response_closed and application close-intent/owner/timestamps; keep primary exception and local-close intent distinct. Never record headers, keys or stream contents.

Preserve legacy error code if API compatibility requires it, but add initiator=undetermined unless directly observed. Do not interpret upstream_transport_error as proof the model provider disconnected.
Document and assert cancel-then-await-before-client-close ownership. A known local close during an active read should carry its actual local cause even when HTTPX surfaces ReadError.

repair_points_after_causal_confirmation.path: confirmed local proxy/transport configuration, if identified
repair_points_after_causal_confirmation.change: Fix only the proven idle boundary or explicit model-route policy after separately authorized controlled validation. Do not change system proxy/TUN, increase unrelated application deadlines, or silently replay accepted unknown model requests.

minimum_followup_regressions: Persist failure-before-cleanup ordering for EOF and close-intent-before-failure for explicit client shutdown, in HTTP and verified TLS.
Run a verified TLS CONNECT proxy relay with a declared short idle-close policy; assert supplier sees downstream close while ModelClient reports unknown protocol outcome without retry.
Run a >50-second no-byte control over direct and nonclosing CONNECT, including a reused keepalive connection; keep the application 300/900-second budgets unchanged.
Exercise manager/child cancellation and client cleanup with event barriers to prove one role does not close another active role/client; never use blind timing races.

Only after the local closing component is identified, validate one explicitly identified real request under frozen input/route/config with correlated request ID and boundary-only trace; do not resend the four unknown requests.
tcp_fin_limit: The first TCP FIN sender is not by itself the TLS/application initiator: a received TLS close_notify or EOF can make the application subsequently send FIN during cleanup. Correlate TLS/read boundary, trace failure and close intent.

fifth_request_supplement.conclusion: For this request, the local proxy port sent TCP FIN before the application. This excludes application-initiated TCP close for this sample; it does not distinguish the proxy policy from a closure originating farther along its selected external transport. Do not retroactively assign all earlier failures an unobserved exact initiator.

diagnostic_recommendation_for_current_fr.reason: b7 evidence is frozen; packet evidence now identifies the fifth loopback initiator. Adding observability does not by itself repair the closing network path.
diagnostic_recommendation_for_current_fr.derive_without_source_change: last_body_idle_ms = duration_ms - stream_last_byte_ms from persisted request observation
separate_future_change: explicit ModelClient.aclose intent/reason/time for active requests
first read failure type/time and preserve primary exception if cleanup fails
initiator=undetermined unless independently observed; never infer from RemoteProtocolError alone

actual_mihomo_loopback_control.controller_access: Read-only Unix-domain /configs, /rules and /connections; bearer secret read from active config only for local controller authentication; never written to evidence.
actual_mihomo_loopback_control.preflight_method: Before any CONNECT, evaluate rules in order for literal 127.0.0.1. Abort for any unknown earlier rule type. First match is index 511 IPCIDR 127.0.0.0/8 DIRECT; no earlier match.
actual_mihomo_loopback_control.process_only_environment: Set HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/ALL_PROXY and lower-case variants to existing local port; unset bypass with empty NO_PROXY/no_proxy; SSL_CERT_FILE points to temporary fixture CA. No system settings or trust store changes.
actual_mihomo_loopback_control.model_client_path: Production app.model.ModelClient; temporary observer subclass records trace and explicit close order without changing stream reads.
actual_mihomo_loopback_control.conclusion: The existing Mihomo local HTTP CONNECT ingress plus its DIRECT route to a loopback TLS server survived 55 seconds without response-body bytes and completed with response.completed and HTTP EOF. A universal 50-second timeout in that local ingress/DIRECT path is not reproduced. This does not exercise the actual external proxy node, its transport, or the remote model endpoint; it does not prove that external chain healthy or uniquely locate the real failures.
actual_mihomo_loopback_control.modifications: No production/test source, live matrix state, daily configuration, proxy rules, system network settings, or system trust modified.

user_supplied_supplier_timestamp_correla.source: User-provided supplier-side disconnect timestamps, relayed by parent investigator; not independently retrieved provider logs.
user_supplied_supplier_timestamp_correla.timezone: Asia/Shanghai (+08:00), as supplied in task context
user_supplied_supplier_timestamp_correla.boundary: The supplied times agree with the local failures to the second, including the fifth failure with proxy-first FIN evidence. No supplier request IDs, raw provider logs, clock-offset proof, or complete provider-side lifecycle trace were supplied. This is temporal corroboration, not a full provider-log audit or an exact component attribution.
